text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) said a series of measures introduced last year to rein in the rapidly growing money supply had been successful and that the M2 figure growth of under 16 percent in 1996 was a positive result.

- The NBS said government investment programmes and the aim of the NBS to keep a stable currency will reduce the amount of resources for commercial credit activities this year. The central bank said that the corporate sector will have to seek other ways of obtaining funds for investment programmes such as direct foreign investment.
- The central bank said it expected commercial banks to take a more cautious approach in their credit activities which should help consolidate the country's trade balance and its current account.
- Tibor Kasiak, head of the NBS banking supervision department, will today formally become head of the Central and Eastern Europe Group of Banking Supervision Comissions.
- The private sector in Slovakia accounted for about 362.8 billion crowns of the total overall industrial output totalling 531.8 billion in 1996, a year-on-year rise of 8.3 percent.
PRAVDA - Foreign Minister Pavol Hamzik dismissed doubts over Slovakia's preparedness for NATO membership, saying such concerns had no rational grounds.

- Jan Slota, Chairman of the junior coalition member, the ultra-right Slovak National Party (SNS), said early elections would solve most of the country's problems and would help decrease social tensions.
NARODNA OBRODA - Jan Borovsky of the minor coalition party, the Workers Party (ZRS), will oppose current leader Jan Luptak for the post of party chairman.
- The government holds its regular session on Tuesday. The preliminary agenda includes a deputies' draft law on the direct presidential elections, but no major economic items.
- Indian steel producer association SAIL is interested in cooperation with the Slovak steel maker VSZ Kosice.
SME - Opposition parties said they would vote against bank privatisation for the second time if the government returns the law barring the sell-off to parliament.
- The ZRS said it would again support the postponement of bank privatisation even if it led to the fall of the government and the breakdown of the ruling coalition.
